heading: Tuesday, August 27, 2024
topLine: Search and reinforcement-learning study settles a 39-year-old Akbulut–Kirby case.

items.headline: Search and reinforcement-learning study settles a 39-year-old Akbulut–Kirby case
items.summary: Shehper, Gukov and co-authors treated the Andrews–Curtis conjecture in combinatorial group theory as a reinforcement-learning environment and applied classical search, RL and language models to it. They showed that one Akbulut–Kirby potential counterexample, whose status had been open for 39 years, is stably AC-trivial. A later version also reports resolving potential counterexamples in the Miller–Schupp series. The trivializations are explicit sequences of moves that can be checked. The preprint was later published at NeurIPS 2025.
